words.gloss: those who are said to be

literal: Those who possess eyes, they say, are the learned; on the face, two sores possess those who have not learned.
translation: Only those who have acquired learning can be said to possess eyes; those who remain unlearned have merely two sores on their face.
modern: கல்வி கற்றவர்களே கண் உடையவர்கள் என்று சொல்லப்படுவார்கள்; கல்லாதவர்கள் முகத்தில் இரண்டு புண்களை உடையவர்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the transformative power of education by redefining physical sight. The author asserts that true sight belongs only to the educated, who can perceive wisdom, truth, and the deeper realities of life. Conversely, the eyes of the uneducated are dismissed as mere physical cavities or sores on the face, as they lack the inner vision that learning provides. The stark contrast between 'eyes' and 'sores' serves to urge the learner to pursue knowledge.
